auraIntro: Explorer, Black Eye Galaxy features a dramatic dark dust band and counter-rotating gas disks from an ancient collision.
overview: The Black Eye Galaxy (M64 or NGC 4826) is an isolated spiral galaxy in the constellation Coma Berenices, roughly 17 million light-years away.
formation: Created by a merger approximately 1 billion years ago when M64 absorbed a gas-rich satellite galaxy rotating in the opposite direction.
structure: A spiral galaxy spanning 40,000 light-years. Remarkably, its outer interstellar gas rotates in the OPPOSITE direction relative to its inner stars and central core.
discoveryHistory: Discovered on March 23, 1779 by Edward Pigott and independently by Johann Elert Bode and Charles Messier.
observationTips: Famous in small telescopes; a 4-inch telescope easily reveals the dark dust patch obscuring the north side of its core.
funFacts: The dark 'eye' feature is a dense band of light-absorbing dust blocking stars behind the core.
Outer gas cloud rotates counter-clockwise while inner stars rotate clockwise due to a absorbed satellite galaxy.
Friction at the shear boundary between opposing gas flows triggers rapid starbirth along a 300 light-year wide ring.

cards.title: Counter-Rotating Dynamics
cards.subtitle: Shear Boundary Starburst Ignition
cards.body: Spectroscopic Doppler shifts confirm that M64's outer gas disk rotates opposite to the inner star disk. The collision boundary creates intense localized star formation.
bulletPoints: Gas beyond 3,000 light-years rotates opposite to inner core.
Collision occurred approximately 1 billion years ago.
Shear boundary compresses gas into hot blue starburst clusters.
